item.title: Six-try Ulster secure bonus point against Zebre
item.description: Ulster run in six tries on their way to a 40-21 bonus-point win over Zebre in Parma to open their European Challenge Cup campaign.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

European Challenge Cup

Zebre Parma (0) 21

Tries: Licata, Ortombina, Montemauri Cons: Giacomo, Montemauri (2)

Ulster Rugby (19) 40

Tries: Walker (2), Stockdale, McCann, Lowry, Moloney Cons: Doak (3), Benson (2)

Ulster ran in six tries on their way to a 40-21 bonus-point win over Zebre in Parma to open their European Challenge Cup campaign.

Recent academy graduate Henry Walker shone on his first competitive start for Richie Murphy's side as he scored two tries for the province and showed great promise in the front row against a tenacious Zebre outfit.

Last season's beaten finalists took a 19-0 lead with Jacob Stockdale also crossing in between Walker's first-half double.

Zebre clawed their way back into the contest in the second half but the visitors finished strongly to keep hold of their bonus point.

Ulster's defence was called into action in the opening exchanges of the game after a set-piece play from a Zebre line-out gave the hosts a dangerous chance before the effort was held up.

In a tightly fought opening 10 minutes, Juarno Augusto also saw an effort held up before Walker got over the line for his first senior try for Ulster on the occasion of his first competitive start.

That score seemed to settle Ulster into a rhythm as they marched up the field six minutes later, only for Nathan Doak's finish to be ruled out for a knock-on after a fine passing move.

Stockdale soon rectified the error from his fellow Ireland international as the Ulster full-back finished off a strong team move in the corner to increase the province's lead to 12.

Zebre's afternoon went from bad to worse when Walker dived over to score his second and Ulster's third in the opening half hour.

By the half-time whistle, Ulster held firm and restricted Massimo Brunello's side in their attacking efforts to merely half-chances.

But Zebre came out swinging in the second half as Giovanni Licata rolled down the short side following a scrum to put his side on the scoreboard before Giacomo da Re converted after 43 minutes.

Four minutes later, David McCann marked his first time captaining the side with a try of his own as Ulster quickly restored their 19-point advantage.

With 15 minutes left of what was becoming a tightly-fought second half, Ulster were put under pressure when replacement Jack Murphy was sent to the sin-bin moments after coming on as a replacement.

The hosts, who are bottom of the URC table, took advantage of their numerical superiority just a minute later as they doubled their try tally through Alessandro Ortombina.

Replacement back Mike Lowry continued the high-scoring for Ulster when he finished off a patient but punishing move after he was found on the left wing and produced a finish worthy of the passing build-up.

For the hosts though, the game was far from over, with full-back Giovanni Montemauri scoring a try that temporarily knocked Ulster out of bonus-point range.

Martin Moloney, who replaced McCann for Ulster, however replied within minutes to restore the crucial three-try buffer and seal maximum points from the trip to the Stadio Sergio Lanfranchi.

With the Challenge Cup now parked until December, Ulster face three consecutive away trips back in the URC, starting with a South African double-header against the Bulls and Stormers.

item.title: Bristol beaten by Stormers in Champions Cup opener
item.description: Bristol Bears lose their Champions Cup pool-stage opener against Stormers, with Jonathan Roche and Leolin Zas both scoring twice for the South African side.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Investec Champions Cup

Stormers (21) 49

Tries: Senatla, Zas 2, Roche 2, Gelant, Venter Cons: Feinberg-Mngomezulu 7

Bristol Bears (7) 12

Tries: Owen, Moody Con: Worsley

Bristol Bears conceded seven tries as they lost to South African side Stormers in their first pool match of this season's Champions Cup.

Seabelo Senatla raced clear for Stormers' opening score and then showed incredible footwork to control a pass with his boot before offloading to fellow winger Leolin Zas.

Joe Owen powered over in the corner to reply for Bristol but Stormers quickly restored their 14-point advantage with a Jonathan Roche try.

Stormers hooker JJ Kotze was shown a 20-minute red card before the interval for making head-to-head contact in a tackle with Bristol skipper Kieran Marmion.

The Bears had spells of pressure while the hosts were down to 14 players either side of half-time. And in a period when Stormers had just 13 men after Zas had been sin-binned for a high tackle, Bristol finally reduced their deficit as Sol Moody emerged from the back of a maul to touch down.

But any hope of a comeback was short-lived as two Bristol players collided when attempting to claim a high kick and Roche collected the loose ball to score his second.

Replacements Warrick Gelant and Andre-Hugo Venter added further scores late on, as did Zas, to secure a bonus point for Stormers, while South Africa fly-half Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu converted all of his side's seven tries.

Bristol, who have won two of their first three Prem games, host Munster in their next Champions Cup fixture on 12 December, before rounding off the pool phase against French clubs Racing 92 and Bordeaux in January.

item.title: Loughnane, 20, becomes youngest champion jockey since 1923
item.description: Billy Loughnane becomes the youngest rider in over a century to be crowned Britain's champion jockey as he collects his trophy at Ascot.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Billy Loughnane became the youngest rider in over a century to be crowned Britain's champion jockey when he collected his trophy at Ascot on Saturday.

Aged 20, the Irishman beat five-time champion Oisin Murphy to the title, becoming its youngest holder since Charlie Elliott in 1923.

Four years after his racing debut, Loughnane won his first Classic in May, the 2000 Guineas, and rode to four further Group One victories among more than 220 wins this year.

"I love my job and I love riding horses – it's all I ever wanted to do," said Loughnane, nicknamed 'Billy the Kid'.

"From the age of six to when I was 12, I used to go racing with my dad [trainer Mark Loughnane] every Saturday to Wolverhampton and I'd be distraught if he didn't have a runner!

"Nearly four years ago when I was going up to Newcastle for my first ride, my aim then was just to have a few winners really. If anyone had said that day that four years later I'd be where I am now I'd have said they were absolutely crazy.

"It's amazing that I've found something that is a passion of mine and to be able to do it as a job as well. Then when you get big success it's even better."

Loughnane's ambitions do not stop here. He is now eyeing Sir Gordon Richards' 1947 record on the Flat of 269 winners in a calendar year and is "not squashing the idea of going for the championship again" in 2027.

Murphy, who went toe-to-toe with Loughnane for a while before the latter strolled to the title, paid generous tribute to his young opponent: "He's got tremendous discipline and work ethic and his results have been outstanding.

"I get on very well with him and I'm delighted to see his success, he's just younger and better looking!"

Meanwhile, it was a memorable afternoon at Ascot for British-Norwegian jockey William Buick who won the Champion Stakes on Ombudsman and the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes on Talk of New York, before completing a 206/1 treble by riding Fifth Column to victory in the Balmoral Handicap.

item.title: Seven-try Leinster too strong for Clermont
item.description: Leinster launch their quest for an elusive fifth European title with an ultimately comprehensive bonus-point win over Clermont at Stade Marcel-Michelin.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Investec Champions Cup pool one

Clermont Auvergne (16) 23

Tries: Jurand, Belaubre Cons: Plummer 2 Pens: Plummer 3

Leinster (15) 48

Tries: Furlong, Sheehan 2, Prendergast, penalty try, Conan, T O'Brien Cons: Prendergast 3 Pen: Prendergast

Leinster launched their quest for an elusive fifth European title with an ultimately comprehensive bonus-point win over Clermont at Stade Marcel-Michelin.

Beaten finalists for the fifth time in eight seasons in May, Leinster head coach Leo Cullen loaded his line-up with Ireland internationals and it paid dividends in a seven-try display in their pool one opener.

While Tadhg Furlong and Dan Sheehan scored first-half tries for Leinster, the hosts edged in front before half-time thanks to Joris Jurand's score and 11 points from the boot of fly-half Harry Plummer.

But a superb try from Prendergast - who scored 16 points - within two minutes of the restart set the tone for the second half as the Irish province pulled away with a penalty try awarded before Sheehan struck for the second.

Mathys Belaubre responded for Clermont before Jack Conan and Tommy O'Brien wrapped up a convincing victory for the four-time champions.

Before kick-off, there was a moment's silence in memory of Lions lock Hyron Andrews, who died on Friday aged 31.

Former Sale player Andrews died at the South African team's hotel a day before their Champions Cup match in La Rochelle.

Clermont have struggled in the Top 14 so far this season with four defeats in six, and their fragility was evident early on when Furlong crossed in the ninth minute after Jimmy O'Brien had gone close for Leinster.

While Clermont responded with a couple of Plummer penalties, Sheehan pounced on the tryline to score Leinster's second after the home side's line-out went awry.

Winger Jurand responded for Clermont, who led by a single point at the break after Plummer nailed a long-range penalty.

Following a testing opening period, Prendergast provided Leinster with a moment to savour early in the second half.

The fly-half, who also impressed in last week's United Rugby Championship win over Cardiff, surged through Clermont and picked out Jimmy O'Brien with a kick. The winger controlled the ball with his foot and gathered before picking out the onrushing Prendergast, who ran in under the posts.

Already wounded, Clermont's hopes were further dented when referee Matthew Carley awarded a penalty try with prop Nohem Ez Zahouany sin-binned.

That was followed by Sheehan's second try, and while replacement centre Belaubre touched down in style for the home side, Conan and O'Brien scores in the final quarter of an hour added gloss to the scoreline for the visitors.

'Our thoughts are with the Lions' - Cullen

Leinster head coach Leo Cullen, speaking to Premier Sports: "Lots of really good stuff in the game. Conditions were a bit tricky, greasy ball, particularly in the first half, and Clermont are a physical team.

"It's a great stadium, great crowd. A sad day of course with Hyron Andrews, our thoughts are with the Lions and all the family connected to them. We only played the Lions a couple of weeks ago so [it was] horrific news to wake up to yesterday morning."

Leinster fly-half Sam Prendergast, speaking to Premier Sports: "It's pretty special [to win]. I haven't played here before, it's an unbelievable atmosphere. The place was hopping, it's a surreal experience as it feels like the fans are on top of you.

"I think a lot of it was forward dominance, our pack was excellent, scrum, line-out defence and maul were very good. That got us into the right areas and that meant we."

item.title: Chelsea's Martinez taken to hospital for 'precautionary tests'
item.description: Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez was taken to hospital as Chelsea's 2-0 win at Everton on Saturday meant they secured their first clean sheet in nine months.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez was taken to hospital for "precautionary tests" after suffering what boss Xabi Alonso said was a concussion during Chelsea's win at Everton on Saturday.

Martinez had earlier played his part in the Blues securing a first Premier League clean sheet in nine months, a run stretching back 23 matches.

But the incident overshadowed an important 2-0 victory for Alonso's side at Hill Dickinson Stadium, secured by two goals from Pedro Neto.

Martinez collided with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite in the 68th minute while attempting to claim a cross from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's free-kick.

There was an eight-minute stoppage before the Argentina international was replaced by Mike Penders, who made his Premier League debut for Chelsea, and saw out the remainder of the match.

Asked about the incident after the match, Alonso said: "It was a concussion, but beyond that I do not know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait.

"What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and is now in hospital undergoing precautionary tests.

"We need to wait. Hopefully it will not be too serious, but at the moment we just have to wait."

There are now doubts over whether Martinez will be fit for Chelsea's next three matches - they face Tottenham and Manchester United in the Premier League, with a Carabao Cup tie at Liverpool in between.

'We need to show we can win in this way'

Chelsea recorded their first Premier League clean sheet for nine months, since a 2-0 win against Brentford in January.

Although Alonso said he was "not obsessed" with keeping a clean sheet, his side, who had conceded a league-high 13 goals before kick-off, were keen to address that record after a much-improved 5-1 win over Bournemouth following the international break.

There had also been discussion about Chelsea being a "soft" team, particularly away from home in the north of England, having lost 19 of their previous 41 matches north of Luton over the past four years.

Last season, Chelsea lost 3-0 at Everton during Liam Rosenior's five-match winless run, a sequence that ultimately cost him his job. The Blues had also won just one of their past nine matches at the Toffees.

This time, however, Everton managed just six shots, their fewest in a Premier League game since recording five against Arsenal last December.

Chelsea also conceded only one clear-cut opportunity and allowed their lowest expected goals against (xG) figure against top-flight opposition this season at 0.45.

They started with a back three of Josh Acheampong, Maxence Lacroix and Levi Colwill, while goalscorer Neto and Jorrel Hato, who provided the assist, operated as wing-backs.

The midfield pairing of Moises Caicedo, returning from international duty, and new signing Jordan Henderson also brought much-needed solidity and experience.

It was £117m club-record signing Morgan Rogers, however, who set the tone for a combative display, squaring up to Everton defender James Tarkowski during an eventful first half.

"We needed to show that we can win in this way," Alonso added. "We looked solid, we played solidly, we were strong and we stayed in control.

"In the first half there were difficult periods with throw-ins, corners and pressure from Everton. You have to overcome those moments.

"In the Premier League it is very hard to have complete control in an away game, but you cannot lose your shape or your conviction."

Who is Martinez replacement Penders?

With difficult matches to come, there will be questions over whether Penders, who became Chelsea's youngest goalkeeper to play in the Premier League at the age of 21, is ready for the demanding run of fixtures ahead.

That concern would be heightened if tests confirm Martinez suffered a concussion, with Premier League protocols typically requiring a minimum 14-day return-to-play process.

Chelsea signed Penders from Genk for £17m in 2024 before loaning him back to the Belgian club. He then spent last season on loan at sister club Strasbourg, where he impressed in both the Conference League and Ligue 1.

Genk have developed a reputation for producing elite goalkeepers, and Penders is frequently compared to Thibaut Courtois by those who know him best.

Like the Real Madrid goalkeeper, Penders stands at 6ft 7in and has recently served as his understudy in the Belgium national team set-up.

He has worked with the same legendary youth goalkeeping coaches, Guy Martens and Gilbert Roex, who also helped develop Koen Casteels, Maarten Vandevoordt, now at RB Leipzig, Lucca Brughmans, who will join Liverpool next summer from Genk, and Nordin Jackers of Club Brugge.

They specialise in developing goalkeepers who are good with their feet, including Penders, who recorded the highest average position while playing out from the back under Rosenior at the Ligue 1 club early last season.

Roex, who has known Penders since his academy days, believes he is capable of matching Courtois' level of success at Chelsea, Atletico Madrid and Real Madrid.

He said: "We have produced a lot of great goalkeepers, but Mike is the one with the potential to reach the same level as Thibaut. His sense of calm is gold in goalkeeping."

item.title: GB's Morris completes hat-trick of golds at Worlds
item.description: Britain's Anna Morris completes a hat-trick of gold medals at the Track Cycling World Championships in Shanghai.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Britain's Anna Morris completed a hat-trick of gold medals at the Track Cycling World Championships in Shanghai as she won the women's madison on Saturday with Erin Boothman.

Wales' Morris, 31, and 19-year-old Boothman, from Scotland, took gold with 40 points - finishing ahead of France in second and Japan in third.

"I am quite speechless. It is going to take a while to sink in and reflect on it," Morris, a seven-time world champion, said.

"It has been a busy few days so now I have got time to let that soak in and enjoy it."

Morris is the first woman to win all three events - team pursuit, omnium and madison - in a single championships since the introduction of women's madison in 2017.

She won the women's omnium on Friday and team pursuit, along with Boothman, Josie Knight and Millie Couzens on Thursday.

England's Couzens, 22, claimed Britain's other gold medal on Saturday, coming out on top in the all-British women's individual pursuit final - beating 29-year-old Josie Knight to the gold by half a second.

Couzens led from the first lap to clock in a time of four minutes 21.505 seconds for her second gold at the championships.

"It is amazing, I am still a bit in shock to be honest. I had zero expectations going in," Couzens said.

Britain lead the medals table with a total of six golds.

item.title: Glasgow get bonus-point win at emotion-filled Sale
item.description: Glasgow Warriors pull away to record an impressive bonus-point victory over Sale Sharks in the Investec Champions Cup at an emotional CorpAcq Stadium.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Investec Champions Cup

Sale Sharks (15) 27

Tries: B Curry, Reed 2, Ma'asi-White Cons: Ford 2 Pen: Ford

Glasgow Warriors (21) 47

Tries: Penalty try, Steyn, Dobie, Craig, Darge, Smith, Tuipulotu Cons: Horne 4, Lancaster

Glasgow Warriors pulled away to record an impressive bonus-point victory over Sale Sharks in the Investec Champions Cup at an emotional CorpAcq Stadium.

Pre-match tears were shed on the pitch and in the stands during a minute's silence in memory of former Sale lock Hyron Andrews, who died on Friday at the Johannesburg Lions' team hotel ahead of their Champions Cup match at La Rochelle.

The 31-year-old played regularly for Sale last season, and his former side started positively as they sought a memorable performance.

Ben Curry peeled off a maul and sprinted through, much to Glasgow's surprise, before Arron Reed crossed out wide after some sharp handling.

However, a penalty try for a maul infringement sent Gus Warr to the sin-bin, before Tom Roebuck joined him after tripping Warriors captain Kyle Steyn.

After Rory Darge spilled the ball with a try beckoning, Glasgow finally took advantage as Steyn raced down the wing to score.

A wonderful finish by Scotland's Jamie Dobie regained the visitors' lead after George Ford's penalty had put Sale back ahead.

Considered one of the favourites to win the tournament after recording a clean sweep of bonus-point wins in last year's pool stage, Glasgow were stunned by Toulon in the quarter-finals at Scotstoun.

One of those wins came against Sale after Franco Smith's side recovered from 14 points down to win 26-21.

Lock Alex Craig powered over from close range as a similar pattern began to emerge, with Rekeiti Ma'asi-White crossing after sustained pressure to keep Alex Sanderson's side in touch.

A sublime one-handed offload from Joe Carpenter then set up Reed to respond to a Warriors maul try.

However, Smith's side, who will be aiming for a deep run in Europe, crossed through replacement Ollie Smith and Ottavio Tuipulotu to secure an additional bonus point.

A new rule in this year's tournament awards an extra point to teams that score three more tries than their opponents.

The second round of fixtures in the Champions Cup will be played in December, with Glasgow hosting Pau and Sale travelling to Dublin to face Leinster.

item.title: McDermott seeks fix as England fight to save their World Cup
item.description: Brian McDermott says he can fix the errors that led to England's Rugby League World Cup defeat by Tonga - but is it already too late?
item.content:encoded:
• Published

As Tonga's deliriously happy supporters celebrated in their thousands in Perth, England knew they only had themselves to blame.

They had passed up plenty of chances to win their 2026 Rugby League World Cup opener and had arguably been the better side for the opening 20 minutes of both halves.

But a succession of mistakes - handling errors, needless offloads, sloppy penalties – allowed Tonga to control the momentum for much of the game.

By the time Haumole Olakau'atu crashed over for Tonga's fourth try in their 30-12 victory, it was all over. The question is whether England's World Cup hopes are also over already.

Not so, insists coach Brian McDermott.

"It was a really good contest, when it wasn't it was down to us and the errors we made," he told his post-match media conference.

"We stood toe to toe for nearly all the game, but we made errors chasing the scoreboard. I'm not going to say it's an easy fix, but it's something I can change.

"We know what is in front of us now. We have to win the next two games. I have seen enough to say we are heading in the right direction.

"We were not strategically outdone. There are tonnes of positives to take out of tonight, but one or two things we must get rid of, like losing possession."

Rugby League World Cup

15 October - 15 November

Australia, Papua New Guinea, New Zealand

Listen to live commentary on every men's match, and key women's matches - with coverage on BBC Radio 5 Live, BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra, BBC Sounds and the BBC Sport website and app

'You cannot play with freedom at international level'

Due to the vagaries of the international rugby league calendar, this was McDermott's first match in charge of England since being appointed in April as Shaun Wane's successor.

Wane had his critics, many of them justified, but he organised a defensively solid England team who whitewashed Tonga on their tour of Britain in 2023.

He left in January after England were well beaten in last year's Ashes, and McDermott has had to piece together a team with minimal preparation.

England did not play a single warm-up match; this was their first game since losing to Australia at Headingley in November 2025. They have not won a match since November 2024, against Samoa.

A much more assured Tonga side started the evening with a spine-tingling Sipi Tau battle dance and ended it with victory for the first time in seven meetings with England.

The relative lack of preparation is out of McDermott's control. Team selection and tactics are not, and that is where the former Leeds Rhinos coach will be questioned.

"You cannot play with freedom at international level, you have to keep hold of the ball," McDermott said after the game. His side looked nervous with ball in hand, too willing to pass up the chance to run at the Tongans and pass the buck.

As for selection, McDermott chose a central pairing of Harry Smith and captain George Williams. They were found wanting, with Williams enduring one of his poorest games in an England shirt.

AJ Brimson was chosen ahead of Jack Welsby at full-back. Although Brimson scored England's first try, he was also caught out of position for Tonga's fourth.

McDermott said he will "have a look" at options regarding selection. Expect changes when the team to face France is named on Tuesday.

"You have to give Tonga credit for the scramble, but I reckon we left three or four [opportunities] out there early doors," said Williams. "We lost our way, we were erratic, we must find that balance to improve the team.

"We can't be kicking stones. We have a great group of lads, and one loss does not change how we think."

Can England still qualify for semi-finals?

But will one loss cost England a place in the semi-finals? The complicated group phase makes that possible.

There are six nations in the combined Group B-C, but all the teams play just three opponents - think a scaled down version of the league phase in football's Champions League. The top two in the overall table reach the semis.

If sides are level on points, head-to-head is the first tiebreaker that will be considered, rather than points difference. But because not everyone in the group plays each other, it may yet be that points difference becomes crucial.

England must win their next two games, against France next Saturday and Papua New Guinea on 30 October, to stand a realistic chance of progression.

If they do, results elsewhere then become a factor - and it could get complicated.

And there is the strong possibility that England will not know their fate for certain until two days later, when Tonga face 2022 finalists Samoa in their last group game.

England's best bet, it seems, is to rack up huge wins in the next two games and hope for the best.

"We want to rack up some points," England wing Dom Young said. "You know, we're good enough to do it."

Maybe England are good enough – but not if they keep making the same mistakes again and again.

item.title: Fatigued Zverev 'overachieved' by reaching Shanghai semis
item.description: Alexander Zverev says he "overachieved" at the Shanghai Masters in reaching the semi-finals amid fatigue caused by his busy schedule.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

World number two Alexander Zverev said he "overachieved" at the Shanghai Masters in reaching the semi-finals amid fatigue caused by his busy competition schedule.

The 29-year-old top seed exited in the last four on Saturday as Spaniard Alejandro Davidovich Fokina pulled off a surprise 5-7 6-4 6-3 win, only his second in eight meetings with Zverev.

Germany's Zverev, who is guaranteed to end the season as world number one, has had little opportunity to rest between the US Open, Laver Cup, Beijing Masters and Shanghai.

"I feel like I've actually, in a way, maybe overachieved this week because of how much tennis I played," Zverev said.

"I carried a little bit of injury, I carried fatigue into the tournament, and I'm OK to lose to a player like this today."

Repeatedly exposed on the forehand side, Zverev surrendered his first break of the match to an exquisite backhand passing shot on the run as Davidovich Fokina took the semi-final to a deciding set.

Zverev was broken to trail 2-0 in the third set and could not recover control of the tie as the 25th seed advanced to his first ATP Masters 1000 final since 2022.

Having failed to replicate the performance which earned him a straight-set win over Alex de Minaur in the quarter-final, Zverev said he has struggled since his fourth-round win over Alexander Bublik went to a third-set tie-break.

"First, I'm not a robot, I'm a human being, I get tired," Zverev said. "After the US Open, I had one day off in total. I think I played a lot of tennis, which is very, very positive because that means I played well.

"I think even here I had tough matches. I personally feel like I was quite flat since the Bublik match, because I was losing energy.

"I played a phenomenal match against Alex de Minaur, but today I was flat. Even in the first set, even though I won the set, I was flatter, I was not reacting so well. I was returning quite badly.

"We're all human beings, even the best players in the world."

His semi-final defeat is a disappointing exception to a brilliant season for Zverev, who claimed the first Grand Slam title of his career at the French Open in June before winning a second at the US Open in September.

Davidovich Fokina will face fellow Spaniard Rafael Jodar in the final on Sunday.

item.title: Chacarra leads as McIlroy fades before play halted
item.description: Eugenio Chacarra extends his lead at the DP World India Championship but Rory McIlroy loses ground before the third round is halted because of darkness.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

DP World India Championship, round three leaderboard

-14 E Chacarra (Spa) (11*); -12 J Luiten (Ned) (12*), A Hidalgo (Spa) (11*); -11 D Hillier (NZ) (14*), A Meronk (Pol) (11*), S Jamieson (Sco) (11*); -10 T McKibbin (NI) (14*), JC Ritchie (SA) (14*), T Clements (Eng) (12*), J Girrbach (Swi) (12*)

Selected others: -9 T Fleetwood (Eng); -8 R MacIntyre (Sco) (13*), D Bradbury (Eng); -7 S Lowry (Ire), L Canter (Eng); -6 P Reed (US) (13*), E Pepperell (Eng) (12*), M Armitage (Eng); -5 A Rai (Eng) (14*) -4 R McIlroy (NI) (15*); -2 J Rose (Eng) (11*)

*Denotes number of holes played before play ended on day one

Eugenio Chacarra extended his lead at the DP World India Championship but Rory McIlroy lost ground before the third round was halted because of darkness.

Spain's Chacarra led by one shot at 10 under after two rounds at the weather-hit event at Delhi Golf Club and sits two clear after 11 holes of his third round.

After successive rounds of 67, the 26-year-old birdied four of his opening seven holes to cement his place at the top as he bids to replace American Patrick Reed at the summit of the season-long Race to Dubai rankings.

Fellow Spaniard Angel Hidalgo and the Netherlands' Joost Luisten are his closest challengers at 12 under, with Scotland's Scott Jamieson a shot further back.

Northern Ireland's Tom McKibbin is four adrift with defending champion Tommy Fleetwood five back after a four-under 68.

Scotland's Robert MacIntyre is also well placed at eight under with five holes of his third round remaining.

However, McIlroy - who sits third in the Race to Dubai behind Reed and Chacarra - fell 10 shots off the lead after an erratic third round.

Having completed a bogey-free second-round 68 early on Saturday, the six-time major winner birdied his opening hole before dropping four shots in as many holes from the third.

After a birdie on the seventh, McIlroy made back-to-back bogeys on the ninth and 10th before sensationally holing out from the bunker for an eagle three at the 14th.

Reed played the first 13 holes of his third round to sit two shots ahead of McIlroy.

The 2018 Masters champion, who tops the Race to Dubai rankings after early-season victories in Dubai and Qatar, mixed five birdies and a bogey before holing his 150-yard approach shot for a spectacular eagle two at the fourth, having teed off at the 10th.

item.title: Professional Ospreys ease to victory in Georgia
item.description: Ospreys get off to a winning start in the 2026-27 Challenge Cup, running in seven tries against Black Lion in Georgia.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Challenge Cup

Black Lion (7) 14

Tries: Spanderashvili, Giorgadze Cons: Tsirekidze 2

Ospreys (22) 39

Tries: Evans, Morse, Sutton, Morgan 2, Lloyd, Hire Cons: Creighton 2

Ospreys successfully avoided a Challenge Cup banana skin with a professional bonus-point win against Black Lion in Georgia.

Mark Jones' men scored seven tries at Avchala Stadium in Tbilisi and limited their hosts to two efforts to secure a bonus point.

Ospreys led 22-7 at half-time after tries by all three members of their back row, Gwilym Evans, Morgan Morse and Huw Sutton, plus wing Luke Morgan.

Further scores followed in perfect conditions for running rugby from Morgan, hooker Lewis Lloyd and prop Kian Hire.

It was a win that would have been even more convincing were it not for Lawson Creighton's struggles from the kicking tee.

Black Lion previously upset Scarlets and French pair Vannes and Montauban, while they pushed eventual winners Montpellier hard in 2025-26, but never threatened the Welsh side.

Ospreys will be relieved to return to Swansea for a pair of fixtures after starting their 2026-27 season with away games in Durban, Johannesburg, Newport and Tbilisi.

They will open their revamped St Helen's home with United Rugby Championship (URC) derbies against Dragons and Cardiff before the November international break.

Travel demands have led to Jones and his staff rotating their squad but the changes did not hinder them in Georgia.

Ospreys took command thanks to two unconverted tries inside 12 minutes, with open-side flanker Evans crossing from a well-worked line-out move and number eight Morse finishing powerfully from a five-metre scrum.

Black Lion struck in the 20th minute through scrum-half Giorgi Spanderashvili, who danced through several weak tackles, but the Welsh side regained control with a close-range effort from blind-side Sutton.

Fly-half Creighton's kicking radar was off but the lead was a comfortable 22-7 at half-time thanks to a botched line-out falling kindly to allow Morgan to go over from Lalakai Foketi's offload.

The second half was a matter of Ospreys protecting their bonus by adding more tries and keeping Black Lion, who offered little other than a formidable scrum, out under new rules in the European competitions.

Morgan acrobatically went over for his second down the left soon after the restart and Reuben Morgan-Williams' fizzed pass put hooker Lloyd in down the other flank.

Replacement prop Hire went over from a yard after centre Owen Watkin's line-break was followed by Lloyd being dragged down just short.

Harri Wilde had a try chalked off by the TMO for offside and the Georgians had the final say through replacement back-row forward Otar Giorgadze from a driving line-out.

Ospreys host Harlequins in December before January fixtures against French opposition at Toulon and at home against Vannes.

Ospreys player of the match Gwilym Evans said:

"We had to start fast because we knew that they pride themselves on their set-piece and physicality.

"We had to match that and wanted to keep the ball in play, moving it about, so we started fast and continued that. We can be happy with the performance."
